subtitle: std::<stdexcept> — the standard exception-class hierarchy: the two bases logic_error and runtime_error (both deriving from exception) and their seven concrete derivatives. Like <new> and <exception>, these are runtime-provided types (the what() string is stored with reference-counted C++ ABI machinery), so restd ships namespace-consistent re-exports (using-declarations) that preserve type identity across the std/restd boundary: catch(std::logic_error&) catches a restd-thrown logic_error and vice versa, and every class is catchable as restd::exception / std::exception. All nine are C++98 in std, so there are no back-ports — the module is a clean 9/9 at C++98. The C++11 const char* constructors come along for free through the re-export. Each class additionally carries a freestanding fallback gated on D_ENV_CPP98_HAS_STDEXCEPT (deriving from restd::exception, storing the message in a non-allocating fixed buffer, exposing the const char* ctor only) so the module never hard-fails. Depends on the restd <exception> module for its base (now shipped); no dependency on <string_view>, and no unmet restd dependencies.
legend_blurb: Per-symbol coverage of the C++ <stdexcept> header. The logic_error / runtime_error hierarchy and its derivatives — all C++98, all re-exported from std with type identity preserved, each with a freestanding fallback. No back-ports needed (already C++98); clean 9/9.

symbols.name: logic_error
symbols.notes: Using-declaration from std::logic_error (base of the logic-error branch; derives from exception). C++11 added the const char* ctor alongside the const string& ctor — both arrive via the re-export. Freestanding fallback derives from restd::exception and stores the message in a fixed 256-char buffer (const char* ctor only).

symbols.name: domain_error
symbols.notes: Using-declaration from std::domain_error (derives from logic_error; argument outside an operation's domain). Freestanding fallback derives from restd::logic_error and forwards the const char* ctor.

symbols.name: invalid_argument
symbols.notes: Using-declaration from std::invalid_argument (derives from logic_error). Freestanding fallback derives from restd::logic_error and forwards the const char* ctor.

symbols.name: length_error
symbols.notes: Using-declaration from std::length_error (derives from logic_error; object asked to exceed its max size). Freestanding fallback derives from restd::logic_error and forwards the const char* ctor.

symbols.name: out_of_range
symbols.notes: Using-declaration from std::out_of_range (derives from logic_error; e.g. at() bounds checks). Freestanding fallback derives from restd::logic_error and forwards the const char* ctor.

symbols.name: runtime_error
symbols.notes: Using-declaration from std::runtime_error (base of the runtime-error branch; derives from exception). C++11 const char* ctor arrives via the re-export. Freestanding fallback derives from restd::exception with a fixed-buffer message (const char* ctor only).

symbols.name: range_error
symbols.notes: Using-declaration from std::range_error (derives from runtime_error; computed result outside representable range). Freestanding fallback derives from restd::runtime_error and forwards the const char* ctor.

symbols.name: overflow_error
symbols.notes: Using-declaration from std::overflow_error (derives from runtime_error; arithmetic overflow). Freestanding fallback derives from restd::runtime_error and forwards the const char* ctor.

symbols.name: underflow_error
symbols.notes: Using-declaration from std::underflow_error (derives from runtime_error; arithmetic underflow). Freestanding fallback derives from restd::runtime_error and forwards the const char* ctor.
